rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thanks so much for offering. A data analyst with a few hours a week is exactly what's useful right now. The first project we're scoping is a Frontier Safety Commitments Tracker: a sourced, dated dataset of the public safety commitments AI developers have made (pre-deployment evals, third-party access, incident disclosure, etc.) and the public evidence on whether each was kept. It's private for now. We'll decide later whether and how to publish it. If you're up for it, a good first ~5 hours would be: 1. Prior-art check (~2 hrs): what trackers or scorecards like this already exist, how current they are, and whether they're maintained. If a good one exists, we'd rather contribute to it than duplicate it. 2. Schema test (~3 hrs): pick one developer and list its public safety commitments (exact quote, source URL, date, conditions), without judging yet whether they were kept. The aim is to find out where the schema breaks. I'll send over the schema and method notes. Tell me if this sounds interesting, or if there's a different kind of work you'd prefer. Best, Morgan (Drafted with help from an AI assistant.)"
rows.quote: Sent: a reply to Priya Raman, who offered to help. It asks her to spend her first ~5 hours checking for existing trackers and testing the schema on one developer. It notes it was drafted with help from an AI assistant.
